general_information.Description: Description: This course helps students to persuade employers, sell ideas to investors and pitch a client for new business. The course also introduces students to the tools and techniques they will need to convince people. For more details, it introduces and examines the STRONG method of pitching, which can be put to use immediately: Setting the Frame, Telling the Story, Revealing the Intrigue, Offering the Prize, Nailing the Hookpoint and Getting a Decision. Lecturer will use several teaching methods such as conducting group discussion and sharing field work experiences in the market on top of regular teaching. Students will have the chance to showcase their presentation and persuasion skills as well as their thinking process related to this field. Teaching methods: Direct Instruction, Inquiry-based Learning, Cooperative Learning, Case Study Analysis
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify basic concepts and principles of pitching ideas effectively
Understand how to create a coherent and captivating presentation out of any content
Understand, demonstrate and analyse methods to structure your content and deliver it with strong body language and personal presence
Enhance the skills to communicate effectively to different audiences
Understand how to alter your message when engaging different stakeholders and end-users
Analyze a variety of persuasive situations using available research and theory
Demonstrate an understanding of persuasive techniques and be able to explain why they work or fail
Evaluate how team roles and processes contribute to team performance
Identify how to act ethically and professionally, and be accountable when professionally pitching an idea

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Students assume they are working for an agency/big corporate and responsible for come up with an idea based on the goal(s) decided by lecturer. This practice is intended to help students to pitch their ideas in order to convince their client/boss that their ideas are worthy and valuable. For the report, the idea pitch must include at least: (1) The goal(s) (2) Target audiences: stakeholders and the end user (3) The big idea (4) Key message(s) (5) The 4 phases (6) Evaluation and discussion (the potential of your ideas) Requirements: The presentation should adhere to the following guidelines: 1. Time limit imposed must be met. 2. All team members must actively participate in the pitch. 3. Presentation should be of professional standard. 4. Pitching theories should be used. Note: Presentations are assessed on the skills explored and developed in the course, including choice of material suited to length and audience, rhetorical structure, use of voice and body, engagement and interaction with audience, and tone and style. Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.Note: Option 1: The mark will be given based on each student's performance in class, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark. Presentation (20) + Report (10%) Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Option 1: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the class; Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Students will be required to pick an advertisement and analyze the advertisement through the lens of one or more of the persuasion theories discussed in class. This practice is intended to help students identify basic concepts and principles of pitching ideas effectively by analysing a key development, change or issue applied to the field of pitching ideas. Through the advertisement, students will learn how to convey their idea to convince their stakeholders. Students will choose a topic from the list provided by the lecturer, or they may provide a detailed topic of their own to be cleared in writing by the lecturer. The topics are intended to justify some of the themes covered in the course and provide them with the opportunity to gain insights into the art of expressing ideas. Requirements: The presentation should adhere to the following guidelines: 1. Time limit imposed must be met. 2. All team members must actively participate in the pitch. 3. Presentation should be of professional standard. Type: Group Presentation Weight: 15% Length: 10-15 minutes/group Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

Type: Group Presentation Weight: 15% Length: 10-15 minutes/group Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
